newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ two-year bonds shed 24 basis points at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ two-year bonds shed 24 basis points at close.

text.p: * NZ mid bonds hold onto gains to end lower
* 10-year yields edge up slightly from open
New Zealand mid bonds continued their impressive rally at Thursday's close, with the 07/98s shedding 24 basis points to close at 7.58 percent.

Shortly before the close SBC Warburg Australia announced that it had issued NZ$75 million of 10/98 bonds in the New Zealand market at 43 points above government two-years. The bonds have a coupon of eight percent.

"There has been a modest amount of interest to buy bonds, concentrated in short to mid term maturities, and the movement in yields has been exacerbated by low levels of liquidity," one bond dealer said.
"There are very few sellers. The buying has come on a market that was not really prepared or in a position to sell, so we've tended to get exaggerated yield movements," he said.

The rally in the 10-year maturities, triggered after they broke through the crucial eight percent level at Wednesday's open, was tempered as the day progressed. They finished four points below last night's closing levels, but six points higher in yield than their open.
Dealers said the next important technical level for the 11/06s was 7.75 percent, followed by their previous low of 6.90 percent.
In the money market, 90-day bank bills and the front futures contracts finished flat.
Dealers said many players had bowed out of New Zealand's debt markets until the general election, due on October 12, had been and gone.

"If you don't know what's going to happen, you shut down your risk and do nothing until you get some new information. A lot of people aren't prepared to do anything even though the yields on the bonds are falling," one said.
